name: Karnika Industries Limited
sector: Children’s apparel design, outsourced manufacturing and distribution; Kidcity retail/B2B channels
summary:
Karnika is a genuine, fast-growing children’s-apparel operating business, but not yet an evidence-backed compounder or an attractive ordinary entry at the stated price. The strengths are an asset-light outsourced production model, a substantial distributor network and recent standalone growth that survives removal of Kidcity’s acquisition contribution. Full-year-adjusted FY23–FY26 revenue CAGR is 19.64%; the latest two comparable standalone half-years grew 60.81% and 37.46%. Those are real positives, not merely a large market opportunity.

The decisive weakness is the conversion of profit into dependable minority-owner cash. FY24–26 standalone CFO/PAT is only 0.336×, falling to 0.067× after interest classified as financing. H1 FY27 group PAT is ₹23.32 crore, while CFO is negative ₹4.41 crore, receivables reach ₹145.32 crore and unsecured loans ₹31.41 crore. Treasury trading, advances and an unexplained March comparative OCI reversal complicate the story.

At ₹133 on 19 October 2026, equity value is ₹824.57 crore. BQS 5.18 and GQS 5.00 are supported analytical points, but G2 Hold excludes quality rankings; IAS is NS. Classification: Hold — unresolved, with material permanent-loss risk. This is an operating-growth and retail-expansion thesis, not a validated compounder. A reconciled auditor-backed reporting bridge and funded collections/refinancing plan would matter more than a lower headline P/E. No ordinary buy price is asserted.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Exact issuer: Karnika Industries Limited, ISIN INE0MGA01012, symbol KARNIKA, active series SM on NSE Emerge. CIN L17299WB2022PLC253035 is preserved as an identifier. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026; price reference is the official 19 October final close, not a live executable quote. There are 61,997,500 issued shares and a verified 1,000-share lot. The five-year research horizon is exactly 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, with a 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle and a clearly illustrative ₹5 lakh position.

G1 is Conditional, not Fail: financial allocation and related-party exposure deserve scrutiny, while clean audit findings and arm’s-length representations remain counterevidence. G2 is Hold because a material same-scope comparative balance-sheet reversal lacks an explanation and bonus-adjusted EPS is presented inconsistently. G3 is Hold pending a current deployability, debt-maturity and collection bridge. G4 is Conditional because complete daily turnover exists but lot constraints, concentration and unknown spreads/queues limit implementation.

Confidence is high on retrieved statement numbers, share count and market tape; medium on normalized organic growth and capital-efficiency proxies; lower on current funding flexibility, retail cohort returns and valuation. FY21–FY22 predecessor results, the 12-day conversion stub, FY23–FY26 standalone and first-year group accounts are kept separate. Unmodified audits are not mistaken for assurance that every later comparative or current funding claim is correct. An analytical cash reserve is not a statutory solvency threshold.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Framework v3.0 weights are unchanged. BQS = 0.20×4 + 0.20×5 + 0.12×8 + 0.10×6 + 0.12×6 + 0.10×3 + 0.08×4 + 0.08×6 = 5.18. Growth Quality Score, not governance quality, has raw GQS = 0.40×8 + 0.20×6 + 0.15×5 + 0.15×6 + 0.10×3 = 6.35. Persistent weak CASH=3 triggers the specific cap, giving final GQS=5.00. The cap is not an extra discretionary punishment on every factor.

IAS uses the final unrounded BQS as Q. Known contribution is 0.25×5.18 + 0.20×3 + 0.10×6 = 2.495, with R and P missing and 55% weighted coverage. Its honest missing-data range is 2.945–6.995; neither midpoint nor renormalized point is reported. R is absent because there is no supported ordinary funded IRR. P is absent because no reliable ordinary price-implied funded crossing is established. D=3 is still supportable from quantified conditional stresses; L=6 is supported by complete daily data.

All 13 factor audits, exact Decimal weights and contributions are retained. CAP=6 uses an actual incremental operating-capital bridge, not a blanket NS or a current ROCE shortcut. BQS and GQS have full factor coverage, but G2 Hold makes all three rankings ineligible. Numerical completeness does not override gate logic.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Karnika designs, sources, manufactures through jobworkers, quality-checks and distributes apparel for children, with management describing an approximately 0–14-year range. Its model is predominantly B2B: distributors, wholesalers, buying houses and retailers take merchandise under Karnika-related brands. Management describes roughly 90% outsourced production, with internal design, cutting, inspection, packing and coordination rather than ownership of a capital-heavy integrated textile chain. Four Howrah facilities are referenced in the latest presentation; earlier address counts are not treated as a capacity expansion without a reconciliation.

Management claims 500-plus new SKUs a month, approximately 540 distributors, more than 2,500 clients and broad Indian coverage. These claims help explain route-to-market access, but are not audited active-customer cohorts or independent market shares. A large own-brand share in B2B invoices does not by itself demonstrate premium consumer-brand economics. Customer credit terms and inventory availability are central: money is collected after sales, so growth can absorb cash even with little factory capex.

Kidcity, acquired at 75% through a fresh subscription in October 2025, adds distribution and retail-facing exposure. Its current shop-in-shop network and the tiny initial kiosk/exclusive-store base should not be confused with the planned 55-plus kiosks. The ₹2 crore investment for 40% in Elementa Lifespaces and the planned small sports-academy subscription are distinct non-core allocations. They are not apparel operating assets to be valued twice. Group accounting includes 25% Kidcity minority interest; parent and group PAT are therefore not interchangeable.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The strongest plausible advantage is a useful local operating system: rapid designs, jobworker coordination, frequent replenishment, distributor relationships and knowledge of affordable children’s apparel. That can reduce retailer sourcing friction and improve inventory availability. It is not yet a proven structural moat. Switching between apparel suppliers is possible; fashion, price, credit terms and service compete simultaneously. Management’s repeat-order and low-return claims do not establish retention by vintage, pricing power or a widening cost advantage.

Three primary-source comparators anchor the limits. Kitex Garments is a much more capital-intensive infant-garment exporter, with FY26 group revenue ₹666.95 crore versus ₹982.80 crore and group PAT negative ₹13.21 crore; parent-attributable profit differs because minority losses are substantial. It demonstrates export/customer-cycle and capacity risks, not a direct Karnika multiple. Brainbees Solutions/FirstCry has FY26 group revenue ₹8,547.94 crore and reported group loss ₹203.66 crore; its company-defined adjusted EBITDA is not interchangeable with Karnika’s core EBITDA. Its multi-channel scale and brand/customer ecosystem are qualitatively much deeper. Monte Carlo has FY26 group revenue ₹1,275.91 crore and PAT ₹112.06 crore, but broader apparel, winter seasonality and store/lease economics differ.

No same-date peer valuation screen or blanket industry P/E is manufactured. The peer filings support business-model and cash-cycle comparisons, not a claim that Karnika deserves their valuation. MOAT=5 recognizes useful, contestable relationships and process advantages. Evidence that would raise it includes retained cohorts with price/mix gains, sustained collections without extra credit, channel-level gross contribution after returns and jobwork, and consumer sell-through rather than distributor loading.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The early operating record is retained rather than discarded because of an IPO. Audited predecessor revenue was ₹47.4641 crore in FY21 and ₹98.8093 crore in FY22. The first company period began on 13 April 2022 and reported ₹124.5924 crore; the audited predecessor stub from 1–12 April adds ₹6.3671 crore. Full FY23 comparable revenue is therefore ₹130.9595 crore. FY24, FY25 and FY26 standalone revenue is ₹127.2726, ₹172.5485 and ₹224.2814 crore. Annual additions from the full FY23 base are negative ₹3.6869 crore, then positive ₹45.2759 crore and ₹51.7329 crore.

The five-year predecessor-to-company CAGR is about 36.4%, but the pandemic trough and change in presentation make it an aggressive measure of sustainable demand. The chosen three-year, full-FY23-adjusted CAGR is 19.64%, starting REV at 7. Using the short company FY23 alone would incorrectly yield 21.65%. The latest two comparable standalone half-years grow 60.81% and 37.46%, supporting the maximum permitted+1 trajectory adjustment to 8. H1 FY26 growth was only 6.04%, so the trajectory is improving rather than uniformly exceptional.

H1 FY27 consolidated revenue 179.9704 versus prior standalone 103.0130 implies 74.71%, but includes Kidcity; underlying standalone growth is 37.46%. FY26 group revenue 248.4790 includes only the post-acquisition period. The ₹24.1976 crore gap to standalone is consolidation contribution after eliminations, not necessarily subsidiary gross sales. A synthetic TTM group revenue of ₹325.4364 crore combines four quarters with Kidcity and is used as a valuation anchor, not an organic-growth statistic. Volume, price and SKU-mix decomposition is not independently quantified; revenue gains cannot all be called unit growth.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Demand access is credible but returns depend on how growth is funded and collected. Distributor penetration, product breadth and Kidcity’s channels create possible expansion. The October call describes 85-plus shop-in-shop locations, but only one kiosk and one exclusive brand outlet then operating. A 55-plus kiosk plan is not 55 operating stores. Management’s ₹0.5 crore annual revenue and 13–14% margin per outlet imply only ₹27.5 crore annual sales from 55 fully ramped outlets before cannibalization and execution effects; that simple capacity arithmetic does not explain all group growth guidance.

The principal reinvestment is working capital, not just machinery. September group inventory ₹62.03 crore plus receivables ₹145.32 crore less trade payables ₹54.22 crore ties up ₹153.12 crore. Even an asset-light model can require substantial incremental financing when credit periods lengthen or retail inventories build. Store fit-outs, staffing, occupancy and returns also matter. Management’s margin and 30–35% growth ambitions remain scenarios, not contracted demand or an automatic funding source.

A full-year-adjusted FY23–FY26 normalized core NOPAT increment divided by core invested-capital increment is approximately 26.55%; the all-capital test, retaining loans and investments in deployed capital while excluding their income from operating returns, is approximately 15.84%. The shorter FY23–25 interval is weaker. Those results justify CAP 6 for mixed deployment: the core franchise can earn good incremental returns, but large financial allocations dilute the economic story. GQS raw 6.35 is capped at 5.00 because multi-year cash realization remains poor. This is not a transitory inventory build inferred from one quarter. Durable growth needs evidence of collections and disciplined reinvestment, not merely a large addressable market.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The promoter family controls 73.39% at the annual reporting date and has long garment-trade experience before the company’s 2022 incorporation. No promoter pledge is reported at that date. Continuity and economic ownership are positives, but do not prove allocation discipline. FY26 related-party sales total approximately ₹30.0492 crore, 12.09% of group revenue. Three promoter executives’ remuneration totals ₹3.60 crore; related rents to them total ₹3.3072 crore. Combined pay and rent are material relative to standalone PAT. The company describes relevant transactions as arm’s length and statutory auditors did not identify diversion; those counterfacts are retained.

Treasury deployment is unusually important for an apparel thesis. FY26 derivatives profit ₹5.0164 crore and insurance commission ₹1.50 crore sit alongside securities losses and large financial investments. Loans reached ₹15.4776 crore in March and ₹31.4123 crore in September; March advances to others were ₹17.90 crore. These are not automatically unrecoverable or related-party abuse, but they compete for capital while the company pays interest and claims growth funding needs. GOV 4 reflects stewardship concerns, distinct from CASH’s collection record and G2’s reporting reconciliation.

Execution credit is given for the completed Kidcity acquisition and realized standalone growth. The September 11 withdrawal of proposed ₹500 crore borrowing/investment/guarantee powers is recorded as a withdrawal based on management’s revised strategic requirements, not as a regulatory rejection or available credit. Main-board migration was only board-approved on October 19 and remained subject to shareholder/exchange processes. The retail rollout and guidance are still work in progress. There is insufficient evidence to invent repeated missed promises; EXEC 6 recognizes delivery while withholding credit for undelivered plans. No bonus-share issuance is treated as economic dilution; warrant conversion is.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The complete statutory audit package was inspected, not just the opinion page. FY26 standalone and consolidated main opinions and separate internal-financial-controls opinions are unmodified. CARO reports no material physical-stock discrepancies or bank-stock/book-debt statement differences, no borrowing default and no identified material uncertainty about obligations as assessed on 16 May 2026. Audit-trail reporting says the facility operated and prior logs were preserved. Latest October 10 standalone and consolidated limited reviews also contain no modified conclusion. These are dated, important counterfacts; they do not independently resolve a later numerical inconsistency.

The material unresolved discrepancy is same-scope March 2026 consolidated comparison: the annual report has investments ₹19.9201 crore, DTA ₹0.8585 crore and other equity ₹34.4202 crore; the H1 filing’s March comparison has ₹22.4304, ₹0.2842 and ₹36.3561 crore. The difference approximately reverses net OCI loss ₹1.9359 crore. September equity rolls forward from the original annual balance using parent PAT and OCI, not from the revised comparison. No explanation was located. This warrants G2 Hold without alleging fraud. By contrast, FY25 Ind AS equity adjustment ₹0.2312 crore has an identified fair-value/tax bridge. FY24 CFO ₹0.1052 crore and FY25 CFO ₹0.8467 crore differences are bounded reclassifications; conservative latest comparatives are used.

Cash quality is weak despite improved core earnings. FY24–26 CFO ₹18.4273 crore against PAT ₹54.8127 crore gives 0.3362×; cash financing interest ₹14.7336 crore leaves ₹3.6937 crore. After net cash capex ₹8.1254 crore, owner FCF is negative ₹4.4317 crore. FY23 company cashflow starts with zero converted opening balances and is excluded from this normal operating test. March standalone receivables older than six months are ₹4.8808 crore versus ₹4.4517 crore prior year; no blanket aging provision is assumed. The group’s September receivables increase ₹57.6381 crore from March while loans increase ₹15.9347 crore. H1 negative CFO is not cured by positive PAT or optional warrants.

Normalized operating EBIT removes all other income, then adds back securities loss, investment transaction cost and identified share-issue cost, retaining jobwork, rent, wages and other real operating costs. A 25% normalized tax is explicitly an assumption. Core and all-capital incremental returns, trade WC/PPE/net-other-asset bridges and capex-minus-depreciation disposal residuals are retained. FY26 normalized standalone profit is still substantially above FY25. Bonus-adjusted FY26 EPS is ₹4.303 standalone and ₹4.510 parent, not printed ₹6.41/₹6.72; comparative FY25 is ₹2.908. The reported time-weighting of a 4:1 bonus would understate the current-share earnings multiple if used without retrospective bonus adjustment.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Valuation starts with the correct share denominator and cash perimeter. At ₹133, market capitalization is ₹824.57 crore. FY26 parent-attributable earnings yield a full-bonus P/E about 29.49×; the first fully consolidated four-quarter TTM parent PAT ₹37.4865 crore gives about 22.00×. Neither is a normalized cash yield. Standalone normalization removes volatile other income and offsets identified noncore losses/costs; it is shown separately rather than treating the subsidiary as valueless or adding its value twice.

The explicit five-year model uses October-to-October periods. Bear/base/bull revenue growth sequences are 5–8%,12–18%, and 15–28%; EBITDA margins 12–13%,16.5–17%, and 18–19%; exit EV/EBITDA 6×/9×/12×. Trade WC, capex, tax, interest, cash, debt, share count, minority claim and noncore recoveries are linked annually. Required operating cash of 2% of revenue is retained at entry and terminal. Negative signed entry reserve deficits are not floored away. Debt rollover is a disclosed assumption, not a verified facility.

All ordinary returns and entry prices are null. Current funding is unverified and non-rescue paths breach the entry reserve. A clearly separate hypothetical exercise of the remaining 75% warrant money supplies ₹35.9993 crore before assumed 0.5% costs and adds 3,966,860 shares. The used 25% deposit is not added again. Issue objects earmark ₹40 crore for working capital and bank/creditor repayment and ₹7.999006 crore for general corporate purposes. The remaining 75% is conditionally allocated ₹30 crore/₹5.9992545 crore, assuming prior use pro rata; that allocation needs a detailed utilization certificate. A tagged annual object ledger applies cash only to eligible vendor/bank payments and business-growth capex/fees within 24 months, with no new lending or speculation. These tags are inside existing cash flows, not extra outflows. On that conditional basis, annual bear/base/bull paths produce approximate five-year IRRs −18.85%,3.45%,17.30%; 15% hurdle entry diagnostics ₹23.27/₹78.36/₹146.82. These are not available buy prices: exercise, refinancing, current assets and reliability remain unresolved. Additional rescue versions disclose gross proceeds, fees and new shares only where a modeled breach requires them. They prefund each interval at its START before uses, sized against both opening and projected closing gaps after excluding the remaining GCP earmark. Net cash uses, reserve growth and GCP release are assumed linear within an interval; seasonal peaks or immediate bullet repayments could require more. Pre-rescue need and breach remain separately visible, so the funded counterfactual does not erase an unfunded shortfall.

The DCF cross-check uses 13/15/17% WACC,3/4/5% terminal growth and 18% terminal incremental ROIC, with reinvestment and cash-reserve growth deducted. Terminal noncore recovery is discounted, not added at entry at full future value. No accumulated operating cash is counted twice. Reverse-expectations bisection retains a real bracket and residual plus cash feasibility; unfinanced algebra is never called a supported requirement. 12/15/18% equity hurdles, margin, receivable days, capex, interest, debt repayment, multiple and portfolio-sale stresses are embedded. Any sold portfolio book is removed from later terminal recovery. IAS remains NS, not the score of the hypothetical rescue.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not that children stop needing clothes. It is that a growing distributor/retail business consumes cash while capital leaves the core for financial investments, unsecured loans and unrelated ventures. Revenue can rise through longer credit and a broader inventory range without equivalent economic profit or cash. A modest slowdown then reveals stale receivables, return obligations and inventory markdowns while short-term borrowing still requires renewal. Treasury gains may reverse at exactly the wrong moment.

The quantified warrant-funded bear case assumes only 5–8% growth,12–13% EBITDA margin, more debtor days and a 6× terminal multiple. Even with hypothetical warrant cash, terminal value per existing investment is roughly 65% below ₹133. The combined stress adds 30 debtor days,4 percentage points of terminal margin pressure relative to the base case, higher capex,12% interest,25% debt repayment and a 6× exit. Annual funding status, any signed deficits and rescue dilution are reported, not hidden behind a target price. Additional equity at ₹133 is itself optimistic in a real stressed market; lower issue prices would dilute more.

The bull counterargument remains credible: strong local distribution and outsourced production can scale with good core incremental returns; quoted investments may be monetizable and undrawn facilities may exist, as management states. Those possibilities are represented in sensitivities, not excluded by fiat. The decision depends on evidence of actual deployability and collections. No observed default is asserted, and the May audit’s no-material-uncertainty assessment is preserved. Thesis-break variables are persistent loan growth alongside negative owner cash, unresolved comparative reporting, a material aged-receivable loss, or inability to fund essential working capital without adverse recapitalization.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A 5× share-price outcome in five years requires 37.97% annual return; 10× requires 58.49%. Neither follows from a children’s-apparel market-size slide. At the current ₹824.57 crore equity value,5×/10× requires approximately ₹4,122.83/₹8,245.67 crore attributable equity before considering future dilution. Fully exercising outstanding warrants expands shares by 6.3984% and dilutes an existing holder by 6.0136%; additional fundraising would raise the required enterprise value further.

Even the modeled hypothetical warrant-funded bull, with very strong growth,19% terminal EBITDA margin and 12× exit multiple, yields only about 17.30% annual return at ₹133. That is far below a 5× path. A higher multiple alone is not a sustainable engine, and guidance cannot substitute for retained owner cash. A full multibagger underwriting would require independently proven retail/distribution cohorts, years of cash-backed growth, disciplined capital allocation and material funding headroom. Present evidence does not support a 5× or 10× base thesis.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Obtain an issuer/auditor reconciliation of the ₹1.9359 crore March comparative OCI/equity reversal and a corrected bonus-EPS denominator. A material unexplained difference persisting in the next filing keeps G2 on Hold.
2. Track standalone growth separately from Kidcity: full FY23 base ₹130.96 crore, FY26 ₹224.28 crore, latest H1₹141.61 crore. Two half-years below 10% without an evidenced mix reason would weaken the trajectory adjustment.
3. Follow group CFO, cash interest and owner FCF, not PAT alone. Baseline H1 CFO−₹4.41 crore; rolling FY24–26 CFO/PAT 0.336×. Sustained ratio above 0.8× with cash interest covered would materially strengthen CASH.
4. Follow receivables ₹145.32 crore and end-balance days, aged balances and subsequent collections. Another 30 days of debtor expansion is a modeled funding warning; a write-off or related-party balance dispute is more serious than a mechanical threshold.
5. Track loans ₹31.41 crore, advances, maturity and repayments. New discretionary loans while borrowing or negative owner cash persists weaken GOV/CAP/BAL; actual timely recoveries strengthen them.
6. Reconcile current available facilities, encumbrance of securities, debt maturities and required peak seasonal funding. Annual claims of generic undrawn lines are not a quantified current buffer.
7. Monitor optional warrants: received 25% already used,75% remaining ₹35.9993 crore. Record cash receipt and issued shares only when exercised; do not front-run planned financing.
8. Monitor outlet openings, closures, aged inventory, same-store contribution and capital per store. Baseline 85+SIS,1 kiosk,1 EBO; 55+kiosks is a target. Sales without store-level cash returns do not validate the rollout.
9. Keep promoter ownership/pledge and related-party flows current; annual 73.39% and no-pledge baseline is not perpetual assurance. Verify actual main-board permissions and revised lot/trading conditions before implementation.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification is Hold — unresolved, with material impairment risk and no ordinary entry recommendation. BQS 5.18 and GQS 5.00 are useful independent assessments of the evidenced business and growth quality, but cannot enter comparative quality rankings while G2 Hold remains. IAS is NS with 55% weighted coverage, not a zero, neutral midpoint or conditional-rescue score. Karnika does not meet the framework’s compounder requirements: GOV 4, MOAT 5, DUR 6, CAP 6, CASH 3 and BAL 4 are below relevant thresholds.

The positive thesis deserves monitoring rather than dismissal: real standalone growth, useful distribution and attractive core incremental economics coexist with accounting and cash concerns. The appropriate next evidence is specific: reconcile OCI/EPS, show current deployable financing and seasonal obligations, collect receivables/loans and demonstrate profitable retail cohorts without uncontrolled dilution. No automatic downgrade merely for SME listing or no access to private bank statements has been applied.

Price matters only after financeability and reliable reporting are established. The conditional warrant-funded base’s 15% hurdle diagnostic is far below ₹133, while the optimistic bull approaches the hurdle; neither becomes an actionable entry range before the assumptions are supportable. A lower quotation alone cannot repair unreliable data or unavailable funding. sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence consists of annual reports, full statutory-audit annexures, predecessor statements, latest reviewed results, acquisition/board filings, earnings calls and official NSE security/tape data. Each retained source has a direct URL, dated scope, hash and location. Management marketing and call claims are labeled; third-party screens were used only for discovery, not as authority for financial totals. Peer financials were checked in their own underlying filings. Raw issuer documents are retained locally but excluded from compact/full analytical backups to avoid distributing shareholder lists and identifiers; backups retain safe financial extracts, source URLs/hashes and reproducible calculations.

Important assumptions include normalized 25% tax,2% revenue operating cash reserve, constant debt unless stressed, no new discretionary loans, no ordinary dividends, modeled trade WC ratios and annual capex, hypothetical warrant timing/costs, minority EV attribution and terminal noncore recovery haircuts. These do not assert restrictions away or establish committed funds. Annual cash paths do not capture every intrayear seasonal peak. DCF terminal assumptions materially influence value and terminal-value shares are reported.

Open questions are the same-scope OCI bridge, correct retrospective bonus EPS, September listed/unlisted and encumbered asset split, current undrawn facility headroom and maturity schedule, recoverability/terms of loans and advances, current customer concentration and collections, retail cohort economics, lease/capital commitments and exact future warrant exercise. Normal consolidation differences, fresh subscription cash remaining inside the group and used IPO/warrant receipts are handled once. Arithmetic reproduction verifies calculation consistency, not fresh source authenticity or future investment performance. This is dated research, not personalized investment advice or a trading instruction.

assumptions_and_limitations: All ordinary returns and entry prices null because current funding is unverified and reliability gate unresolved.
Required cash 2% of revenue is an analytical safety reserve, not a statutory minimum or evidence of default. Even zero extra capital cannot erase a negative signed reserve deficit.

Debt held constant except explicit sensitivity; refinancing and facility availability not established. No further loans advanced, portfolio speculation, dividends or discretionary acquisitions assumed. This is optimistic capital-allocation discipline, not a promise.

Warrant exercise at entry is counterfactual timing; outstanding 75% exercise optional, existing 25% deposit used, assumed 0.5% incremental costs. Issue objects specify 40 crore working capital including creditors/bank repayments and 7.999006 crore general corporate purposes including issue expenses. Remaining cash is conditionally allocated pro rata 30 crore/5.9992545 crore, requiring proof of prior 25% utilization by object; no automatic legal flexibility assumed. Tagged eligible payments consume earmarks within 24 months without adding cashflow twice. GCP capex use is a business-growth assumption requiring confirmation; no lending/speculation funded.

General rescue issues at unchanged INR 133 and 2% fees solely to quantify funding need; real stressed price/availability may be worse. New holders dilute existing holders; no automatic loan/asset monetization.

Additional rescue is hypothetical prefunding at each interval START, never retroactive year-end financing. Its size covers opening and projected closing gaps after GCP earmarks. Net uses, required reserve and GCP release are assumed linear within intervals; this is not verified seasonal liquidity or a promise of timely issue proceeds. Pre-rescue funding need and breach remain visible separately.

Terminal NCI claim assumes 25% ownership of subsidiary contributing 20%/25%/30% group EBITDA, hence 5%/6.25%/7.5% group EV and excess cash. All consolidated debt charged to parent is conservative; no second subtraction of NCI book equity. Actual subsidiary earnings/capital split needed.

Noncore financial investments include associate book value once; loans/advances haircuts are terminal recovery assumptions, not current financing. No separate property value, no added IPO proceeds, restricted FD not treated as free cash.

Asset-light apparel economics: trade working capital, vendor outsourcing, sell-through, debtor days and retention matter more than plant utilization. Retail ramp requires inventory, leases and staff; capex ratios include operating retail reinvestment but lease obligations are not fully separable.

DCF retained cash reserve deducted at entry and reserve growth deducted in annual and terminal cash flows; accumulated cash not added again. Terminal reinvestment at 18% incremental ROIC is an assumption, not CAP proof.

liquidity.status: 60 of 60 sessions observed. Starting L=7 for 2.503 reference days; one-point downgrade to 6 for INR 133,000 minimum lot, concentrated float and sparse whole-lot capacity at 2% participation. Spread and queues not observed; no execution guarantee.
